h1: ILR changes in 2026: what the earned settlement plans mean for you
title: ILR Changes 2026: Earned Settlement Explained | UVS
description: The government plans to move most routes to a 10-year earned settlement model. What the ILR changes mean, what is not yet law, and what to do now.
intro: The government has announced plans to change how people qualify for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR). These ILR changes could mean waiting longer for settlement, but they are not law yet, and the current 5-year routes remain open.

sections.heading: What has been proposed?
sections.text: The government plans to replace most 5-year routes to ILR with an "earned settlement" model. Under its proposals, the standard qualifying period would rise to 10 years. People who meet certain contribution criteria, such as higher earnings, could qualify sooner, while people who have claimed public funds could wait longer.

sections.heading: Is any of this in force yet?
sections.text: No. The proposals are not yet law, and the existing 5-year routes to settlement are still open. The government has said it will publish the final rules, including any arrangements for people already in the UK, later in 2026. It has also said the changes are intended to apply to people already on the path to settlement.

sections.heading: Who could be affected?
sections.text: Most people on routes that currently lead to ILR after 5 years could be affected, including many Skilled Worker visa holders. The government's proposals indicate that partners of British citizens would keep a 5-year route, but the final rules haven't been published.

sections.heading: What should you do now?
sections.text:
If you are eligible for ILR now, or will be soon, the safest approach is to apply as soon as you can. Before applying, check:
- Your exact qualifying date
- Your time outside the UK, which for most routes must be no more than 180 days in any 12-month period
- Your Life in the UK test and English language evidence

Our free absence calculator on our ILR page lets you check your trips in a couple of minutes.

faqs.a: The government has proposed a 10-year standard qualifying period, but it is not law yet. The 5-year routes remain open for now.

faqs.q: Will the ILR changes apply to me if I am already in the UK?
faqs.a: The government has said it intends them to, but the final rules, including any transitional arrangements, have not yet been published.
